note: rAF ticks faster than 60 Hz here, so the frame-budget answer is framesOver16_7ms (a frame longer than 16.7 ms missed a 60 fps deadline), not the median.
The board is deliberately NOT virtualised: all 540 tiles are mounted at once.
Every motion interaction added by this pass -- hover lift, press scale, the refusal shake, the ticking counts -- runs inside budget with 540 tiles on screen.

Horizontal scrolling misses frames, and the last two rows isolate why: with the identical DOM and JavaScript but nothing painted the same scroll costs 8.4 ms instead of 29.2 ms, and removing every ticking count changes nothing. The cost is the browser rasterising newly revealed columns of a 17-column, 540-tile board -- paint, not animation. No motion change can move it; windowing the columns would, and that is a structural change outside a motion pass.
